title: The Shoreline Where Pressure Becomes Testimony

features.name: chalk agreements
features.desc-on-touch: You run your hand over salt-scored stone where names and dates mark the tide's slow settling. The chalk has faded but the pressure remains.

features.name: tide pool testimony
features.desc-on-touch: The pool holds still water and the compressed record of a hundred tides. Small stones rest on its floor, each one marked.

features.name: salt crust deposit
features.desc-on-touch: Crystalline layers build here where the shore learned to preserve pressure as salt. Each stratum a record of compressed force.

features.name: weathered pressure post
features.desc-on-touch: The post has been abraded smooth by decades of sand and tide. It still stands, bent slightly by the force it has taken.

features.name: agreement arch
features.desc-on-touch: Two rocks have leaned against each other so long they have grooved into shape. The shore carved this arch from the act of bearing witness.

features.name: shore-learned marking
features.desc-on-touch: Pale stones arranged in patterns the tides have not yet erased. You can almost read what they mean.

inscription: here the shore learned the language of pressure and began to answer back

reverie.title: REVERIE — shoreline at dusk, where agreements are kept
narr: You stand at the edge where the tide won't reach tonight.
She moves along the rocks, marking names with pale chalk,
agreements the shore itself will witness. The light fails gold.
You both know the tide will take these marks, but that's
the point — the shore doesn't keep the writing. It keeps
the act of someone who came here and agreed to stay.
